quests.title: Something For The Headaches
quests.description: Deliver 1 Fine-or-better Healing Draught to Mira so she can treat the town's growing wave of stress and sleepless pain.

completion_milestones.title: First Town Relief
completion_milestones.text: Mira's first delivered draught changed the conversation in the square. The tower is no longer just a ruin above town. It has begun helping again.

quests.giver_intro_line: If you really mean to work that tower, help me first. Half the square comes to me tired, aching, and pretending they are not worn thin. One proper healing draught. Something I can hand over without a speech about managing expectations.
quests.giver_active_line: Steady enough for real sleep. I do not need it pretty. I have three people waiting who will not sit down.

quests.title: A Safer Walk Home
quests.description: Deliver 1 Excellent Glow Potion with the soft_glow trait to Rowan so the darkening road home feels safe again.
quests.giver_intro_line: I work the cuttings after dark now. The beds do better when nothing is watching them, which is a stupid thing for a herbalist to say out loud. Bring me a light I can carry between the rows and I will stop saying it.
quests.giver_active_line: Any light yet? I have been counting the rows by touch and I keep getting a different number.

quests.title: The First Living Bed
quests.description: Deliver 1 Fine Glow Potion after the greenhouse opens so Brin can wake the old planter wards and give the town one reliable growing space again.

completion_milestones.title: Greenhouse Expanded
completion_milestones.text: Brin reset the old planter wards. A new moon bed is active on the north side of the greenhouse, and the town finally has reason to believe the valley can recover in more than scraps.

quests.giver_intro_line: The greenhouse beds are dead ground with glass over them. Give me one cultivation brew that actually works and I will show this town that growing here is still a skill and not a superstition.
quests.giver_active_line: Still waiting on that brew. The beds are not getting any younger and neither, frankly, am I.

quests.title: For The Work Crews
quests.description: Deliver 1 Fine Stamina Tonic with the quickstep trait to Mayor Elric so the town crews can keep up repairs without collapsing early.
quests.giver_intro_line: What worries me is not one bad season, it is the pattern. Thinner beds, shorter tempers, crews tiring at noon. Make me one disciplined stamina tonic and I will have something to put in front of a council that has spent nine years calling your tower a hazard.
quests.giver_active_line: Disciplined, mind. If it is wild I will be defending it rather than presenting it.

completion_milestones.title: The Crews Kept Working
completion_milestones.text: Elric put one tonic in front of the council and the repair crews finished a week's work in four days. Nobody voted on anything. It simply became harder to say the tower was a hazard while standing on a road it had helped rebuild.

quests.title: Proof The Tower Once Healed
quests.description: Deliver 1 Star Lantern Elixir to Ione so she can prove the tower's old work reached beyond its own walls.
quests.giver_intro_line: I have nine years of notes on a tower I have never been inside. Bring me something the observatory records actually describe and I can start checking my work against the thing instead of against itself.
quests.giver_active_line: Whenever you have it. I have waited nine years; I can manage another fortnight without becoming unreasonable about it.

quests.title: Gentle Habitats
quests.description: Deliver 1 Beastcalm Extract so Lyra can tune the habitat wards and begin steadying the valley's unsettled small creatures.

completion_milestones.title: Habitats Stabilized
completion_milestones.text: Lyra tuned the habitat wards. Gentle collection from tower creatures can now support regular alchemical work.

quests.giver_intro_line: The small creatures are changing their habits. Fewer pollinators, stranger nesting, too much fear where there used to be routine. Give me something calm enough to tune the wards with and we shelter them properly, rather than trapping them and calling it help.
quests.giver_active_line: Calm, and it has to carry light. I am not putting anything sharp near them while they are already frightened.

quests.title: The Beds That Will Not Take
quests.description: Deliver 1 Fine-or-better Purified Draught to Rowan so she can flush the seed trays and find out whether the fault is in the seed or in the ground under it.
quests.giver_intro_line: Now that I can see them, I wish I could not. Four trays sown the same week and not one of them has taken. I need something clean enough to flush the trays without leaving its own residue behind — then at least I will know whether to blame the seed or the ground.
quests.giver_active_line: The trays are waiting. Nothing clever, mind. Clean. Whatever you bring me becomes part of the answer, so it had better not be part of the question.

completion_milestones.title: The Fault Is In The Ground
completion_milestones.text: Rowan's flushed trays came up as empty as the sown ones. The seed is sound. Whatever is failing in the valley is failing underneath it, in ground the town has worked the same way for four generations.

quests.title: What The Valley Used To Grow
quests.description: Deliver 2 Fine-or-better Verdant Restoratives to Rowan so the bed rows behind the square can be turned and fed properly for the first time in years.
quests.giver_intro_line: The ground, then. It has been asked for a harvest every year and offered nothing back since before my mother had the stall. Two restoratives, properly made, and I will turn the whole bed row myself. If it works we stop buying our own herbs from the road traders.
quests.giver_active_line: Two of them, and neither one thin. I only get to turn those beds once this season — if the second is weaker than the first I will have wasted the row and the year with it.

completion_milestones.title: The Bed Rows Turned
completion_milestones.text: Rowan worked the restorative into the bed rows behind the square and had the whole row turned before evening. Within days there was moss on the north wall again and bloom along the path. The town square grows its own for the first time in a decade.

quests.title: Count What Is Still Flying
quests.description: Deliver 2 Fine-or-better Mothlight Brews so Lyra can mark the bloom rows after dark and count what still comes to them.
quests.giver_intro_line: The wards hold and nothing is breeding. Sheltered, fed, safe, and not one new brood since I opened the floor. I need to know whether that is happening out in the valley too, and I cannot count what I cannot see. Two mothlight brews. I will mark the bloom rows and sit with them after dark.
quests.giver_active_line: Two, so I can mark two rows and compare them. One row on its own tells me a number. Two tells me whether the number means anything.

completion_milestones.title: The Count Is Taken
completion_milestones.text: Lyra sat two marked bloom rows for four nights and counted eleven visitors where her predecessor's log recorded ninety. The collapse is not in the tower's habitats. It is the whole valley, and the habitats were only where it became impossible to ignore.

quests.title: Something Worth Coming Back For
quests.description: Deliver 1 Excellent-or-better Bloomrise Elixir so Lyra can work a full season of flowering into the valley's bloom rows at once.
quests.giver_intro_line: Eleven where there were ninety. They did not die, they left, because there was nothing here worth the trip. So we give them one. A bloomrise elixir, and I mean a real one, worked into the rows all at once so the whole valley flowers in the same week. Either they come back for that or they do not come back at all.
quests.giver_active_line: It has to be a morph, and it has to be excellent. Anything less and the bloom is a week early and a week thin, and I have spent my one chance at it.

completion_milestones.title: The Valley Flowers At Once
completion_milestones.text: Every bloom row in the valley opened inside four days. By the end of the week Lyra had stopped counting visitors and started counting broods. The habitats have a third occupant now, and the wild rows have more bloom than anyone alive has walked through.

quests.title: Too Many, Too Alike
quests.description: Deliver 1 Excellent Mirrorsalt Draught to Mira. She needs something provably clean to test the town's water against.
quests.giver_intro_line: I have been treating these headaches for two years and calling it strain. Then I wrote out who came in, and when, and it is the same street, the same week, the same complaint. That is not strain. That is a source. I need something I know is clean to measure the water against, and mirrorsalt is the cleanest thing anyone brews.
quests.giver_active_line: Excellent or it is worthless to me. I am not comparing the well against something that might itself be off.

completion_milestones.title: The Same Street, The Same Week
completion_milestones.text: Mira measured the square's water against a mirrorsalt pour and stopped writing halfway through. The headaches are not stress and never were. Everybody who came to her counter drank from the same well.

quests.title: Everyone Who Drank From It
quests.description: Deliver 2 Fine-or-better Fieldwide Poultices to Mira so she can treat the whole affected street at once instead of one patient at a time.
quests.giver_intro_line: It is the well, and it has been the well for two years, and I have been handing out single draughts to people who go home and drink from it again. I need something that treats a street. Not a patient. A street. Two of the wide poultices, and I will walk the row myself.
quests.giver_active_line: Two. I am not choosing which half of the street gets treated and then explaining that choice at this counter for the rest of my life.

completion_milestones.title: The Well Row Treated
completion_milestones.text: Mira walked the well row in one afternoon and treated every house on it. Within a week her counter had gone quiet for the first time since she took it over, and she has started stocking for a town that plans rather than one that copes.

quests.title: Twice, The Same
quests.description: Deliver 2 Excellent Purified Draughts to Mayor Elric. The council will not sign for work that might have been luck.
quests.giver_intro_line: The council does not doubt that you can do it. They doubt that you can do it twice. Bring me two purified draughts of the same grade, brewed apart, and I can argue that the tower is a supply rather than a series of favours. A town cannot budget for favours.
quests.giver_active_line: Two, both excellent. One excellent and one merely good makes their argument for them, and they will enjoy making it.

completion_milestones.title: Entered In The Ledger
completion_milestones.text: Two draughts of matched grade went in front of the council and the tower stopped being an anecdote. It has a line in the town ledger now, which Elric says is the only kind of trust that survives a change of mayor.

quests.title: The Last Dark Mile
quests.description: Deliver 2 Excellent Nightwatch Lanterns to Mayor Elric so the watch can hold the outer road after dark.
quests.giver_intro_line: One thing left. The outer road goes dark a mile before the last house and the watch will not stand it, which means nobody moves goods after dusk, which means the whole valley trades on somebody else's timetable. A lantern that lights when a man stops walking and holds all night. Two of them. Then we are done being a town that closes at sundown.
quests.giver_active_line: Two, and they must be excellent. A watchman does not get to relight anything at the far end of a dark mile.

completion_milestones.title: A Town That Does Not Close At Sundown
completion_milestones.text: The watch took the outer road and held it, and the council put the tower's supply into standing orders rather than one-off requests. The board in the square carries the town's business now, not its emergencies.

quests.title: Whatever Is Left Under The Wall
quests.description: Deliver 2 Fine-or-better Greenmend Salves to Brin so he can find out whether anything under the tower's old terraces is still alive.
quests.giver_intro_line: There are terraces cut into the slope under the tower wall. Nobody has put a fork in them since before I started, and I have walked past them twice a day for thirty years assuming they were rubble. Two greenmend salves and I will find out whether that assumption was work or laziness.
quests.giver_active_line: Two, because I want to try the north terrace and the south one. They get different light and I have been guessing about that for three decades.

completion_milestones.title: Still Alive Under There
completion_milestones.text: The tower's terraces are not rubble. Under two feet of fallen mortar Brin found bed structure, drainage channels and root stock, laid out by somebody who understood the slope better than anyone working the valley today.

quests.title: Somebody Knew What They Were Doing
quests.description: Deliver 1 Excellent Deeproot Tonic to Brin so the tower's terraces can be brought properly back into work.
quests.giver_intro_line: Whoever cut those terraces knew this slope better than I do and has been dead or gone for twenty years. I would like to finish their work rather than start my own. One deeproot tonic, the slow kind, because a terrace is not a season's job and I am not going to treat it like one.
quests.giver_active_line: The slow kind. Anything that works fast will have worn through before the first winter and I will have wasted the only chance the slope gets.

completion_milestones.title: The Terraces Worked Again
completion_milestones.text: Brin brought the tower's own terraces back into cultivation, following the original bed lines rather than laying his own. The ruin edge grows again, and he has taken to calling the person who cut them 'the previous groundskeeper', which is the highest thing he says about anybody.

quests.title: Somebody Took The Pages Out
quests.description: Deliver 1 Excellent Marginalia Lantern to Ione so she can raise what was scraped off the floor logs before they were sealed.
quests.giver_intro_line: Eleven months are missing from the floor logs. Not lost — removed, cleanly, by someone who knew which gatherings to take and left the binding intact so nobody would count. There is scraping under the last surviving entry. I need a light that raises what is no longer strictly on the page, and I am told the tower can make one.
quests.giver_active_line: Excellent grade. A weak one will show me that something was written and not what, and I would rather keep the not-knowing than have it confirmed and still be useless.

completion_milestones.title: Under The Scraping
completion_milestones.text: The erased hand came up faintly under the marginalia light. It is the wizard's, it is unhurried, and it is a working note rather than a confession: eleven months of somebody quietly proving to themselves what the tower would do if it were left running.

quests.title: Check It Against The Thing
quests.description: Deliver 1 Excellent Hollowroot Cordial to Ione so the recovered pages can be tested against something they describe.
quests.giver_intro_line: The recovered pages describe a cordial made from a plant that does not exist. I have spent nine years being careful not to believe things I could not check. Bring me one and I will have done, for the first time in my career, the thing I keep telling other people to do.
quests.giver_active_line: One will do. I am not testing a supply, I am testing a claim, and a claim only needs to be checked once to stop being a claim.

completion_milestones.title: The Record, Reconciled
completion_milestones.text: Ione measured a hollowroot cordial against the description on a page that had been scraped blank for twenty years. They match. Her nine years of notes now have a foot in something outside themselves, which she says is the difference between an archive and a collection of opinions.

completion_milestones.title: The Eleven Months
completion_milestones.text: The removed gatherings are legible enough to file. They cover the season before the sealing: yields falling, wards drawing more than they returned, and the same three words in the margin of four separate pages — 'not yet, then'.

completion_milestones.title: The Previous Hand
completion_milestones.text: Somebody removed those eleven months deliberately, and it was the wizard, and they did it after writing them. Ione's reading is that the pages were taken out not to hide the decision but to stop anyone finding the working that led to it and being persuaded by it.

quests.title: A Station Nobody Can See
quests.description: Deliver 1 Excellent Nightwatch Lantern to Tarn so the waystation at the top of the pass can be seen from the road at dusk.
quests.giver_intro_line: The lamp here died before I took the route and nobody has been up to relight it since, because why would they. A carter coming over at dusk sees nothing, so a carter coming over at dusk does not stop. One lantern that holds all night once a man stops walking, and this becomes a station again instead of a wall.
quests.giver_active_line: Excellent grade or do not bother. It is going up a pole in the wind at the top of a pass and nobody is going to be relighting it.

completion_milestones.title: The Waystation Relit
completion_milestones.text: The lamp at the top of the switchback is burning again for the first time in over a decade. Two carters stopped the first night. Tarn says that is how a road works and the only way it works.

quests.title: The Animals Come Over Worse
quests.description: Deliver 2 Fine-or-better Stillkeeper Tonics to Tarn for the animals that come over the pass too spent to eat.
quests.giver_intro_line: Everyone worries about the carters. The carters are fine; they chose this. It is the animals that come over the top shaking and off their feed, and a mule that will not eat at the waystation is a mule that does not make the next one. Something settling. Two, because they do not come over one at a time.
quests.giver_active_line: Calm, not strong. I am not trying to make them work harder. I am trying to get them to put their head in a bucket.

completion_milestones.title: Heads In The Bucket
completion_milestones.text: Tarn has started keeping a settling tonic at the waystation as standard. The carters have noticed their animals arrive at the far side in better condition than they leave the valley, which is not something anyone can remember being true.

quests.title: The Four Months Nobody Crosses
quests.description: Deliver 2 Excellent Hardwinter Draughts to Tarn so the pass can be worked through the winter instead of closing behind the valley.
quests.giver_intro_line: Here is the thing nobody down there says out loud. The pass shuts for four months and your valley spends a third of every year on the wrong side of it, and you have all arranged your lives around that as though it were weather rather than a decision. I am told you can force a frostcrack seed open out of season. If a seed can be argued with, so can a road.
quests.giver_active_line: Two, and both excellent. One gets a crossing started. Two gets it finished, which is the half that matters.

completion_milestones.title: The Pass Kept Open
completion_milestones.text: The switchback was worked through a full winter for the first time in living memory. The valley spent no part of this year cut off from anywhere, and the only people who found that unremarkable were the ones who had never known it any other way.

quests.title: Three Of The Same
quests.description: Deliver 3 Serviceable-or-better Healing Draughts so Wren can stock the infirmary shelf with bottles that behave identically.
quests.giver_intro_line: Three healing draughts. Serviceable is fine — I would rather have three serviceable than one excellent and a shrug. When somebody comes in frightened I need to hand them a thing I have handed somebody before and watched work.
quests.giver_active_line: Three. Not two and a promise. The third one is the one that makes the first two mean something.

completion_milestones.title: Three Of The Same
completion_milestones.text: Wren has three identical draughts on the infirmary shelf, which is the first time in nine years the row has held more than one of anything. She said the word 'stock' out loud twice and then apologised for it.

quests.title: The Ones Who Cannot Sleep
quests.description: Deliver 2 Fine-or-better Calmleaf Infusions for the patients Wren cannot treat with anything stronger.
quests.giver_intro_line: Two calmleaf infusions, and Fine this time, because the people they are for have already been given the cheap version by somebody who meant well. Half of what walks into that corridor is exhaustion wearing something else's coat.
quests.giver_active_line: Two. There are two of them and they are both in the second room, and neither has slept properly since the spring.

completion_milestones.title: The Second Room
completion_milestones.text: Both patients in the infirmary's second room slept through. Wren logged it in one line and underlined the date, which for her is an outburst.

quests.title: The Shelf She Stopped Keeping
quests.description: Deliver 1 Excellent Purified Draught with the pure trait — the last bottle Wren needs before she can clear out the shelf she has kept for twenty years of worst cases. She will only take it from a hand that has mastered the formula.
quests.giver_intro_line: There is a shelf at the back I have never explained to anybody. It is what I keep for the cases I cannot fix, so that I have something to do with my hands while somebody dies. One excellent purified draught and I can take it down. But I want it from someone who has made that formula so many times they could do it badly and would still not — a good bottle by luck is the thing I am trying to stop needing.
quests.giver_active_line: The back shelf. I have not touched it in four months, which is the longest since I started keeping it, and I would like to stop counting. Take your time and get the formula under your hands first; I have waited twenty years.

completion_milestones.title: The Shelf At The Back
completion_milestones.text: Wren cleared the shelf she kept for the cases she could not fix. She did not make a speech about it. She moved the bottles, wiped the board, and wrote the day's stock on it instead, which is a different kind of record entirely.
